title: Dynamic canary rollback safeguard with traffic-conditioned eval probes
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a traffic-conditioned canary gating service that runs lightweight, cohort-aware eval probes during canary and A/B rollouts and triggers automatic rollback policies when statistically significant regressions are detected. Key goals: minimize blast radius for model/config changes, avoid false positives from noisy traffic, and provide a soft-fail fallback mode that keeps critical paths online while investigating regressions.
acceptance_criteria: A canary rollout can be initiated with 'traffic_probe=true' and targets a configurable set of cohorts
For each probe window the system computes configured metrics (e.g., perplexity delta, top-k agreement, safety score) and a composite quality score using weighted aggregation
If composite score crosses the configured regression threshold for a configured consecutive-window count, an automated rollback trigger is emitted and executed within SLA
System records provenance for each decision (input sample set, metric snapshots, cohort weights) and surfaces it in the console rollback event
Soft-fail fallback: when rollback is not immediately possible (e.g., infra constraint) routes degrade to a lower-tier compatible model variant and emit an incident ticket automatically
End-to-end tests simulate drift and validate rollback within tolerated time for 95% of synthetic test cases

decisions: Use traffic-conditioned sampling (cohort + request fingerprint) rather than global sampling to preserve signal where user behavior is heterogeneous
Adopt sequential testing (CUSUM) with configurable drift sensitivity instead of single-window p-value tests to reduce noisy-trigger rollbacks
Composite quality score will be weighted aggregation of user-defined metrics; default weights: correctness 0.5, latency-effect 0.2, safety 0.3
Rollback action defaults to full revert, with configurable 'soft-fail' that routes failing traffic to a compatible lower-cost model variant if revert is blocked
Provenance required for all auto-rollbacks and persisted to retention window of 90 days for audits
